inspiration: Team colour as a reserved palette index range: 16 indices (80 to 95) are set aside for the player colour, and remapped from one chosen colour (palettes.yaml:47; PlayerColorRemap.cs:18-38). Recreate: a 16-step team ramp in our sprite palette so one colour pass recolours trim and cloth, not the whole sprite.

Remap math in linear colour space: the chosen team colour is turned into hue, saturation and value once, and only the reserved indices change (PlayerColorRemap.cs:29-38). Recreate in the sprite shader: convert to linear first, then remap, then convert back, so bright trims do not go muddy.

Fog of war as three source states: passive visibility, shroud and active visibility (OpenRA.Game/Traits/Player/Shroud.cs:74). Shroud (never seen) and fog (seen, not now) are separate palettes and separate sprite sets, with a fallback fog index for art that is not fully fogged (ShroudRenderer.cs:35, :57). Recreate: explored ground stays drawn, units do not.

Shadow as a fixed palette index (ShadowIndex: 3, 4) on every terrain palette (palettes.yaml:6, :16). Recreate: flat ground shadow as two reserved palette indices, no separate shadow art; cheap at 375 wide.

One palette per biome with the same shadow and remap indices: temperate, desert, snow, interior (palettes.yaml:2 snow; :12 temperat; :17 desert; :7 interior). Zone-as-data idea: change the biome palette, keep the rest of the sprite pipeline. Biome palette swap for zones.

Unit definitions by inheritance: the 20 top-level vehicle definitions in mods/ra/rules/vehicles.yaml each carry an Inherits line; the first inherits from a base template (vehicles.yaml:2). Catalogue pattern for row 21 (catalogue fields): one base template per class, small overrides per unit.

Localisation as keys (actor-<id>-name) in Fluent files, about 769 key-value lines in the RA set (mods/ra/fluent/rules.ftl:95). Pattern for our copy: stable ids in code, text in files, no hard-coded names.

Colour picker that reuses the same remap indices, so the player sees the colour on a unit sample (ColorPickerPalette.cs:44; palettes.yaml:44-47). Pattern for guild or team colour choice in the client menu.

briefs.label: Team-colour trim on a grey-clad soldier
briefs.why: A reserved 16-step ramp recolours only trim and cloth, so each side reads at a glance at 375 wide, with no second sprite per colour.
briefs.keep: a reserved index range for the team colour; one chosen colour per player; a linear-space remap done once
briefs.change: our own 16-step ramp and shade steps; trim on armour and belts, not the whole body; a ring glow in our colour, not the donor's

briefs.label: Remembered fog over explored ground
briefs.why: Explored ground stays visible but empty of units, so the player keeps the map and loses the live picture; a fallback fog art index covers tiles with no fully fogged art.
briefs.keep: three source states (passive, shroud, visible); separate shroud and fog palettes; a fallback fog index
briefs.change: our own fog ramp and mist texture, not the donor's; a soft edge in our style; a faint outline on explored roads

briefs.label: Desert palette swap for a zone
briefs.why: A biome palette with the same shadow indices changes the feel of a whole zone with no new sprites; the rest of the pipeline stays the same.
briefs.keep: one palette per biome; shared shadow and remap indices; swap by zone data
briefs.change: our own biome colours and sky tint; fewer, bolder palette steps; add a heat shimmer effect rather than a sand texture
